title: Course exercises, 2011 to 2017
summary: The class exercises behind the bigger projects: VB.NET forms, Flash pieces, OA and object-oriented examples, SQL for a registration system, VC++ assignments, Android basics, Java programs, ERwin data modelling, and C problems.

title: One game per new language
summary: My rule as a student, from a club senior's advice that the textbook for a new language is making a game: every new language gets a game with a made-up company logo on it. C, C++, Java, Android and Unity each got one.

title: BLUE DICE GAME
summary: A two-player dice race on a 19-square board in Visual Basic 6, my first university team project (five students; I planned the program).

title: BNI's Cafe board site
summary: A cafe-style bulletin board built three times: an HTML frameset home page, a Classic ASP version with members and admin pages, and a PHP version with member ranks, per-rank read, write and delete rights, replies and password recovery.

title: DHTML calculator
summary: A web calculator with digits, operators, clear and backspace, evaluated with eval, plus a short write-up.

title: Lotto number picker
summary: A lottery number picker written three times while learning each language: a VB.NET form for a class, then a Win32 window program, then a Java Swing version.

title: Mukbo DB
summary: A C++ console maze game from an OOP course: steer DB through the map and eat every piece of bread. Monsters and stage select were never finished. Its title screen already said BNI Tech.

title: Number base converter
summary: A small Windows form that converts numbers between bases.

title: Rolly Poly
summary: An unfinished two-player property-trading board game in VB.NET by a team of three; I wrote the ranking and buy screens.

title: Teris
summary: A console Tetris in C with hold, combos and a two-piece preview. In 2026 I came back to it and ported it to macOS.

title: Study repositories
summary: Code written to learn, not to ship: C pointer and data-structure studies (where Teris started), a game club's Unity study, coding-test practice, a daily learning log, and book examples on Kotlin, Spring Batch, Spring REST Docs, Kafka, React and building an LLM.

title: Campus guide
summary: A Flash app for parents, new students and visitors: pick a start and a destination and a character walks the path to the building; it also finds restrooms, ATMs and departments. A five-person graduation project; I led the team.

title: PHP sign-up and login pages
summary: Sign-up form, login, profile editing and duplicate checks for id and phone number, built step by step as a course report.

title: Space Shooter
summary: A Galaga-style shooter in C++ on the plain Win32 API with double-buffered GDI drawing; one stage is playable. The art was redrawn for this release.

title: Shell phone book
summary: A menu-driven bash script that keeps a phone book in a file, in two versions.

title: Snack vending machine design
summary: A class design for a vending machine: pick candy, noodles, snacks or drinks, see the description, enter a quantity, watch the balance, get change at any time. Three or more classes required; no code is kept.

title: Bookstore manager
summary: A bookstore program with a login window and tabs to search, edit and add or remove books by ISBN, title, author, category, publisher and stock. The edit and add tabs stayed empty.

title: PackMan plus
summary: A Java Swing maze game: eat every coin while robots roam, with items and three difficulty levels. The art was redrawn for this release.

title: Piano app
summary: An Android class exercise: eight note images that play an mp3 when tapped.

title: Ajotchi basketball matching app
summary: Online basketball communities lived in cafes with no app, so this one matched teams and opponents by location, let players register and like courts, and kept pickup teams and friends for the next game. A five-person contest team; I led it.

title: Angry Pokemons
summary: An Android side-scrolling action game, an unofficial student fan game. The characters and music are removed from the published code.

title: ESC: Enjoy Suwon Culture
summary: An Android app that put Suwon's community-centre culture programs, from the city's open data, on the phone. Passed the first round of the city's open-data contest. A three-person team; I led development.

title: Motorbike rental
summary: One of six app candidates for a public-data contest in 2015. Only the title survives.

title: What to eat nearby
summary: A nearby-food app, one of six public-data contest candidates in 2015. Only the title survives.

title: Full parking lot
summary: One of six public-data contest candidates in 2015. Only the title survives, and what it meant was not written down.

summary: A route-finding app, one of six public-data contest candidates in 2015. Only the title survives.

title: Look after my own health
summary: A health app, marked lower priority among six public-data contest candidates in 2015. Only the title survives.

title: Protect our baby
summary: An infant-safety app, marked lower priority among six public-data contest candidates in 2015. Only the title survives.

title: WarmyLand
summary: A first-person 3D exploration adventure on a penguin planet, built by a three-person university game club team. I led the Unity development.

title: 3D Maze
summary: A 3D maze escape game in C++ and OpenGL with three camera views, made by a team of three; I wrote the game code.

summary: An entry on a 2021 side-income plan, marked not started.

summary: A take-home assignment for a technical product role at a game company: sequence diagrams and script problems, answered in a slide deck.

summary: A repository meant to collect computer-science notes in AsciiDoc. Only the table of contents was written.

title: WDYW

title: Video editing
summary: One line on a 2021 list of things I wanted to do. No subject or format was written down.

title: LMK
summary: Three service skeletons in one go, a core API, a webhook receiver and a web app, one commit each. What LMK stands for is not recorded.

summary: A diary note from 2025: game development was my childhood dream and one reason I joined a game company; maybe Canada is where I try it. No concrete plan.

summary: A personal app for people who visit skin clinics: treatment records, passes, points, payments and treatment cycles in one place, with a skin quiz and three languages. Someone else's app; my part was a security review and the Play release preparation.

title: Claude done-notification hook

title: GitHub profile as an AI-work portfolio
summary: My GitHub profile rebuilt to show how I work with Claude Code: five public repositories, a map of how they connect, and a page of five working rules with evidence.

summary: This page: my ideas, works and content from 2011 to today, rebuilt every day from data files. Started in 2026-03 as an empty ideas document and became a site in 2026-10.

title: git workflow commands
summary: Slash commands for the branch, pull-request and commit rules I kept repeating: push a branch the right way, clean up merged branches. A README-update command was retired in 2026-10.

title: notebooklm command
summary: A slash command that sends outside content to NotebookLM through a CLI and returns a structured analysis.

title: dooray-analyze
summary: A Claude Code skill that pulls Dooray tasks and wiki pages through a CLI, keeps the originals and writes an insight analysis of each.

title: Personal knowledge system
summary: A plan to rebuild the structure of a company knowledge system on my laptop. Only the first stage was done; it was dropped the day the LLM wiki started.

title: claude-config
summary: My Claude Code setup as code: instructions, skills, hooks, scripts, memory and launchd jobs in a private git repository, restored onto a new machine by one bootstrap script.

title: dawndeck
summary: A personal start page for the laptop and the phone: city clocks and weather, an exchange rate, wiki search, spaced-repetition cards for English and CS, countdown banners and an expiry radar. Visitors read, the owner signs in.

title: dooray-task-post
summary: A slash command that creates Dooray tasks with content written to a set of rules.

title: Drive output archive and audit
summary: A rule and a check: everything Claude produces for me goes into one Drive folder tree, readable from any device, and a command scans every session transcript for documents that were left outside it.

title: english-practice
summary: A Claude Code skill for everyday Canadian English: free talk, drills and message checks, with every correction and suggested phrase kept in a Drive corpus. A phone route lets a chat on the go land in the same corpus.

title: english-review
summary: A skill that turned my tutoring archive and a Canadian phrasebook into Leitner review cards and watched their quality. Card-making stopped in 2026-10; the archive continues.

title: LLM wiki
summary: A private knowledge wiki that Claude reads and maintains: topic, entity and source pages built from YouTube, the web and keyword research, cross-checked before they are written, with a lint script.

title: Two-laptop setup
summary: A way to send Claude work from a portable laptop to an always-on one at home, with machine identification hooks. Retired when the second laptop was sold.

title: wiki-ingest
summary: A Claude Code skill that takes a URL or a topic through capture, a skeptic's cross-check and composition, with two human review gates, and adds the result to the wiki.

title: Departure checklist
summary: A 51-item checklist in seven groups, planned backwards from a departure date: luggage by bag, documents, things to cancel, expiry dates while abroad, and a checked-baggage weight budget.

title: Household ledger
summary: Actual spending kept as one CSV per month (date, currency, amount, category, item, payment method, note) with rules for the columns, compared against the plan.

title: Persona debate lab
summary: A method for developing an idea in a meeting of job-based personas with me in the room, scored later against what actually happened. The method, the roster and the counts are public; the transcripts are not.

title: at-keyboard
summary: A command that estimates whether I am at the laptop from the last keyboard or trackpad input and the screen-lock state, for sessions driven from a phone.

title: jd-analysis
summary: A skill that reads a job description or a recruiter message, judges the employment structure first, records it in a numbered ledger and builds a tailored résumé per application, reviewed twice before it is published as a document.

title: vancouver-log
summary: A skill that keeps diary-style entries about life in Vancouver exactly as told, backfills past days, checks settling-in progress and keeps a separate list of writing seeds.

title: whereami
summary: A small macOS app and command that print where the laptop is: coordinates, accuracy and an address. Started after a location guessed from memory was 4.5 km off.

title: 23-day English sprint
summary: A study plan for the 23 days before a move: no new material, three sessions a day (speaking from cards, listening, role play), with unfriendly role plays that interrupt and ask back.

title: Vancouver room hunt
summary: How I found a room share in Vancouver with Claude Code: the skill that searched and scored listings by total monthly cost, and the field notes behind it.

title: daily-routine
summary: A weekly routine with a place and a time slot for each part of the day, and a cloud routine that posts the day's plan to Discord at 05:00 with three Canadian English expressions, plus a study guide page built from the same data.

title: dev-experience and career-facts
summary: One ledger of what is true about my engineering career, a derived fact sheet that other skills read instead of re-analysing sources, and the only skill allowed to write either.

title: interview-roleplay
summary: A skill that runs a mock interview in English for one role, one stage and one interviewer persona, then debriefs in Korean.

title: interview-script-review
summary: A skill that checks a prepared self-introduction or answer against my recorded facts, Canadian interview norms and how it sounds spoken.

title: job-search
summary: A skill that scans LinkedIn, Job Bank and company boards for new developer postings, removes what was already seen, ranks the rest and posts a phone-readable board to Discord.

title: Studio job watch
summary: A scheduled task that reads the career pages of a few game studios every day and reports new postings to Discord and Drive.

title: Score recorded English calls
summary: Record my English phone calls, score each one and compare it with the next to track my level. Past calls were scored once; no repeating setup was built.

title: Transcript keeper for video links
summary: Give it a YouTube or Reels link and get the English transcript with a Korean translation, kept in one place; study-method videos become HTML notes. Done by hand inside sessions, never built.

title: Eight-week listening and shadowing program
summary: Silent listening, retelling, dictation and shadowing with one TV drama, scheduled by weekday and by where I can make noise. Eight weeks from 2026-09.

title: AI trend digest
summary: A daily digest of AI developer news to Discord, collected from RSS, Hacker News, GitHub trending and Reddit and written by a Claude cloud routine.

title: AI news service
summary: An idea for a service with today's news, recent AI stories and recommended content: Reddit and live trend topics in, NotebookLM for analysis, Obsidian to keep it, Claude tying them together.

title: branch-band
summary: A Claude Code plugin that shows the current repository and branch above the prompt, in red on main, for checkouts shared by several sessions.

title: Career dashboard
summary: A claude.ai dashboard that reads my Drive markdown records each time it opens, so it is current without republishing.

title: career-counseling
summary: A skill for private career conversations whose notes stay in one owner-only folder and reach no other tool or record.

title: coding-practice
summary: I solve LeetCode problems by hand with no AI; Claude reads my submission history, commits the code under my name alone, drafts notes under its own mark and keeps the progress table.

title: dawn-guard
summary: A Claude Code plugin that denies risky deletes, commits and pushes on main, commits without a co-author line, and mail sending or deletion before they run, and lets a command through only after I confirm. It denies when it cannot decide.

title: email-manage
summary: A skill that labels a mailbox by an agreed scheme, reports the mail that matters first and drafts replies. It never sends or deletes; I do that.

title: experience-posts
summary: A skill that writes English posts about my real engineering work into a private repository first, unfiltered, and publishes a filtered version later.

title: Recruiter question drill page

title: secret-redact
summary: A Claude Code plugin that masks webhook tokens, API keys and private keys in what the screen draws, so a session can be watched from a phone or shared.

title: transcribe-rec
summary: A command that turns a screen recording or a call recording into a timestamped transcript and a frame sheet.

title: Auto-publishing blog with ads

summary: Keep each answer cs-prep has checked as one card file: the question, a short English answer, sources and version, traps, and a pointer to the record behind it, read from the career dashboard.

title: engineering-notes
summary: English posts about work I actually did at two companies, in a public repository that stands in for a portfolio site. An unfiltered private original comes first; the first draft is written.

title: github-profile skill
summary: A Claude Code skill that owns everything I show on GitHub: the profile README, this organization and its page, and each public repository's README and visibility.

title: Interview English track
summary: A weekly plan for interview English: write answers to technical and computer-science questions three days a week, say them aloud the other three, and three quick questions every day.
